chapters.title: A meeting on the water
chapters.body: Kushner’s family trip brought him to Albania. In Rama’s later account, an invitation aboard a yacht in Durrës introduced the two men. Reporting dates the encounter to summer 2021.
chapters.limit: This is a retrospective account. The host’s identity is not consistently established; the meeting does not prove a financing arrangement.

chapters.title: The conversation turns to investment
chapters.body: According to the Financial Times account relayed by Politiko, a later conversation at Davos touched on Albania and investment opportunities.
chapters.limit: The exact date of this meeting is not established here. An expression of interest is not an agreement.

chapters.title: A return visit
chapters.body: Kushner returned with a larger group, including Richard Grenell. The same account describes a week of visits and explicit interest in investing.
chapters.limit: A visit establishes neither land ownership nor project approval.

chapters.title: Sazan enters the approval process
chapters.body: AIDA’s information-request register refers to Decision 23 and applicant Atlantic Incubation Partners LLC. Reuters reported strategic-investor status for the Kushner-linked proposal.
chapters.limit: Strategic status is not a land deed or a construction permit. The complete signed decision and ownership chain remain outstanding.

chapters.title: Two places. Different decisions.
chapters.body: The government’s June account distinguishes Sazan from Zvërnec: Sazan remained state property without a final agreement then. For Zvërnec it cited a 30 March development approval and 15 May environmental decision.
chapters.limit: This is the government’s account, not an independent inspection of every permit. Sazan and Zvërnec must not be treated as a single land transaction.

chapters.title: From the coast to the streets
chapters.body: OSW traces the environmental demonstrations to 30 May. By October, reporting describes broader student demands about education, living costs and accountability.
chapters.limit: Political support does not prove control of the movement. No reliable central financing account has been established here.

records.title: Tirana incinerator: the award and the money
records.body: The Open Procurement register records an 8% evaluation bonus approved on 7 December 2016, one bidder, Integrated Energy B.V., and an offer of ALL 17,139,106,821 excluding VAT. The 30-year award is dated 24 August 2017; contract 6021 Rep., 2894 Kol. is dated 31 August 2017. The contracting authority was the Ministry of Environment.
records.limit: A bonus or a single bidder does not itself prove an offence. The offer is not the amount ultimately paid; performance, amendments and expenditure need separate records.
records.subject: Integrated Energy

records.title: Who owned the incinerator company in 2022?
records.body: The registry-derived profile for Integrated Energy BV SPV (L72031013B) lists Dutch GeoGenix BV, formerly Integrated Energy B.V. (66671752), as its 100% parent. Its reproduced beneficial-owner extract effective 10 May 2022 identifies Alberto Presezzi at 40%, Max Abitbol at 20% and Dominique Marcelle Obadia Abitboll at 20%. Another 20% is not individually identified in that extract.
records.limit: These are historical indirect interests, not certified current ownership. Klodian Zoto’s former administrator role in 2016–2018 does not establish current ownership. Preventive seizure in 2023 and the January 2026 administrator listing for Indrit Karaj are separate legal facts.
records.subject: GeoGenix

records.title: Llogara: three procurements must stay separate
records.body: SPAK’s 20 November 2025 statement describes proceeding 136/2025 and alleged interference involving Belinda Balluku and five procurement-committee officials: Evis Berberi, Gentian Gjyli, Erald Elezi, Jetmira Dervishi and Mirzeta Kashnica. The construction tender ceiling was ALL 18,967,810,952 excluding VAT.
records.limit: A ceiling is not a payment and allegations are not convictions. Reuters reported further formal charges on 20 October 2026 and Balluku’s denial. The separate 2021 supervision tender and reported 2025 A-M/Gjoka maintenance award (about ALL 230m over four years) must not be attributed to the construction case without evidence.
records.subject: Belinda Balluku

records.title: Sazan: applicant, status and missing agreement
records.body: AIDA’s 2025 register of information requests and responses refers to Strategic Investment Committee Decision 23 of 30 December 2024 and Atlantic Incubation Partners LLC (EIN 92-3329707). It is an information-request register, not a complete strategic-investment or ownership register. Reuters reported strategic status for the proposed Kushner-linked resort.
records.limit: The signed decision, annexes and full ownership chain have not all been independently inspected. The registered agent Corporation Service Company is not thereby a beneficial owner. Strategic status is not proof of a completed land sale or construction.
records.subject: Atlantic Incubation Partners

records.title: Sazan Operations and the Al-Khayyat ownership report
records.body: BIRN’s April 2026 reporting on QKB records describes Sazan Operations, founded 1 April 2026, as controlled through six companies by Ramez and Mohamad Al-Khayyat. It reports five unnamed Albanian investors holding 24% of Blue Industries Investment Holding BV, an entity in the related structure.
records.limit: That 24% must not be depicted as a direct stake in Sazan or Atlantic Incubation Partners. Kushner’s precise personal equity and the complete chain between project vehicles remain unverified. Citizenship and family connections do not establish state control or wrongdoing.
records.subject: Sazan Operations

records.title: Sazan and Zvërnec have different land and permit questions
records.body: In its June 2026 explanation, the government said Sazan remained state property and no final agreement had then been signed. Its account of a 30 March development-permit approval and 15 May in-depth environmental assessment requirement concerns Zvërnec. Legal and technical conditions still governed issuance of the development permit.
records.limit: This is the government’s dated account, not an independent cadastral audit or a construction permit. Obtain each parcel, land title, environmental decision and final agreement separately. Citizens.al’s account of ten negotiation meetings led by Elira Kokona and reported state demining costs require minutes and expenditure records.
records.subject: Sazan / Zvërnec

records.title: Durrës Marina: public assets and the project vehicle
records.body: The Port Authority records a 10 August 2022 memorandum between Eagle Hills, represented by Mohamed Alabbar, and Albanian Seaports Development Company, represented by Erlis Hereni. Research also identifies a reported 67%/33% project-vehicle split and a historical 40.18% indirect Alabbar interest in Eagle Hills.
records.limit: The latter percentages remain registry-verification leads in this release. The public return requires the signed agreement, land valuation, tax treatment, guarantees and accounts. No evidence reviewed establishes an award-for-contract exchange with the UAE presidency.
records.subject: Eagle Hills

records.title: The Albanian Files: an architecture research starting point
records.body: The publisher lists The Albanian Files: Freedom and Architecture (2026), edited by Anneke Abhelakh, with an Edi Rama foreword, 60 architecture studios and 796 pages. Its relevance is the selection of architects, development finance, land and public benefit.
records.limit: The book itself has not been fully reviewed. Do not assume Sazan or Zvërnec appears in it. For every project, establish the developer, selection procedure, land parcel, permit, environmental review, completion stage and public costs before drawing a conclusion.
records.subject: The Albanian Files

records.title: Poverty: corrected source version and estimates
records.body: The World Bank brief downloaded for this review is labelled October 2026. It estimates poverty at the $8.30/day line (2021 PPP) at 25.0% in 2024 and 23.1% in 2025, with a 21.6% projection for 2026. It says subsequent figures are model estimates because the latest household survey used for this measure is from 2018.
records.limit: This replaces the draft’s 23.8% for 2024 and October 2025 label. International poverty, national poverty and relative at-risk-of-poverty are different measures. The Macro Poverty Outlook provides wider economic context, not evidence of individual criminal responsibility.
records.subject: World Bank

records.title: Governance, corruption perceptions and media freedom
records.body: Transparency International’s rule-of-law brief cites Albania’s 2024 CPI score of 42/100 and rank 80. RSF’s 2026 country page ranks Albania 83/180 and describes conflicts between business, politics and media. Freedom House’s 2025 assessment combines competitive elections and assembly freedoms with corruption and polarisation concerns.
records.limit: CPI measures perceptions; a rank is not a count of offences. Freedom House’s 2025 edition mainly concerns 2024. TI’s brief carries an April 2026 publication date despite its 2025 title. These are institutional assessments, not judgments against a named politician.
records.subject: Governance indices

records.title: ACER, European Commission, Amnesty and ECRI
records.body: ACER’s CMS 2025 summary reports 59% saying they paid a bribe and 54% saying one was requested. The European Commission’s 2025 report records both anti-corruption and organised-crime enforcement progress and continuing weaknesses. ECRI lists its seventh Albania report as adopted 17 March and published 17 June 2026. Amnesty’s 2025 world report contains an Albania chapter.
records.limit: ACER’s denominator, reference period and questionnaire need the full methodology before interpreting these as population-wide rates. ECRI and Amnesty are included as source dossiers; this release does not claim to have completed their recommendation-by-recommendation analysis.
records.subject: European Commission

records.title: Health, EBRD and historical CIA data: verification gaps
records.body: The draft’s WHO claim that noncommunicable diseases accounted for 66.6% of 2021 deaths could not be reproduced from the dynamic country page. The EBRD transition-assessment page did not yield its substantive text in this retrieval. The cited CIA 2021 archive URL redirected to a Factbook retirement notice.
records.limit: These remain source leads, not newly verified indicators. No numerical conclusion is drawn from a successful HTTP response or a page title alone.
records.subject: Health / development datasets

records.title: WikiLeaks, the leaked OSCE report and Offshore Leaks
records.body: OCCRP’s account of a November 2009 US diplomatic cable concerns the Berisha period, before Rama became prime minister. Its separate report on a leaked OSCE document distinguishes authentication of the document from substantiation of allegations it repeats. ICIJ’s public Offshore Leaks database provides partial records for identity-matched research.
records.limit: A diplomatic assessment is not a court finding. The leaked report does not establish the alleged €200m offshore fortune. Offshore incorporation is not itself illegal; similar names and country filters cannot establish an individual’s identity or guilt. Draft ICIJ result counts are not treated as fixed findings.
records.subject: Leaked records

records.title: MEK relocation began under Berisha in 2013
records.body: The US State Department’s 18 March 2013 statement welcomed Prime Minister Sali Berisha’s offer to accept 210 former Camp Ashraf residents temporarily at Camp Hurriya, with UNAMI and UNHCR cooperation. The source link has been corrected. Later expansion under Rama and the Ashraf-3 context belong to the subsequent timeline.
records.limit: This establishes the initial offer and international support, not all later terms, expenditure or alleged MEK operations. It does not establish that Israel ordered the relocation.
records.subject: MEK relocation

records.title: Iran: technical attribution in 2022 is not attribution of 2026 protests
records.body: FBI/CISA’s AA22-264A advisory documents Iranian state-linked destructive cyber operations against Albanian government networks in 2022. AP separately reported Albanian authorities’ attribution of the February 2024 INSTAT attack to HomeLand Justice.
records.limit: Neither record proves that Iran organised October 2026 demonstrations. A new attribution needs identified accounts, operators, payments, communications and independent technical evidence. Online amplification, even if established, does not invalidate protesters’ grievances.
records.subject: Iran cyber attribution

records.title: Foreign interference: separate political claims from technical evidence
records.body: Rama publicly alleged Iranian and Russian online amplification and invoked Antifa and anti-Israel or anti-Trump actors. NDI’s foreign-interference study discusses vulnerabilities and narratives, rather than proving a common command structure for these protests. BIRN reporting on the police’s October statement describes investigations of online threats without public identification of a foreign state operator.
records.limit: No independently reproducible state-attribution dataset was identified in the reviewed material. June environmental demonstrations and October student/civic protests require separate evidence. Religious identity or ideological overlap is not an organisational or financial link.
records.subject: Foreign-interference claims

records.title: Viral foreign-police images and flight claims
records.body: RFE/RL reports Faktoje’s identification of an AI-generated image used to allege foreign police involvement, police denials, manipulated material about buses from Greece, and Tirana airport’s denial of extra flights from Israel during the protests.
records.limit: Debunking a particular image or flight claim does not identify who created it. It also does not disprove every possible foreign influence allegation. Each original item needs a dated, separate check.
records.subject: Viral images

records.title: Bektashi sovereignty and the national-interest test
records.body: Rama’s proposed Bektashi sovereign entity is a documented proposal. Assess secularism, religious equality, constitutional procedure and territorial implications separately from the Sazan, Zvërnec and Durrës projects. The reviewed records do not establish a shared agreement linking these initiatives.
records.limit: A proposal is not an enacted founding instrument or a precedent establishing another state. Test each policy through its democratic mandate, published risk assessment, net public costs, measurable benefits and alternatives; no single hidden plan is established.
records.subject: Bektashi proposal

records.title: Swiss neutrality is a policy comparison, not Albania’s legal position
records.body: Albania joined NATO on 1 April 2009. Its collective-security commitments differ from Switzerland’s permanent neutrality. The research asks whether foreign-policy choices offer measurable humanitarian, diplomatic, economic and security benefits proportionate to their risks.
records.limit: Neutrality is not the absence of sanctions, diplomacy or refugee protection. The comparison is a political alternative to analyse, not evidence that Albania is legally required to follow Swiss policy.
records.subject: NATO membership

records.title: Honours, organisations and official roles
records.body: Public event accounts document Rama’s CAM Global Leadership Award (September 2024, with the Center for Jewish Impact), Vital Voices recognition (December 2021), Sesame Workshop’s Joan Ganz Cooney award (June 2022), and Israel’s Presidential Medal of Honor (April 2025). Sherrie Westin was identified as Sesame Workshop President at the 2022 event. UAE officials also announced the Order of Zayed in January 2026.
records.limit: Award-giving and attendance do not establish private payments, ownership or procurement favours. CAM’s Sacha Roytman/Natan Sharansky, Robert Singer and Vital Voices’ Alyse Nelson/Hillary Clinton are organisational context, not financial edges. Albania’s 2020 OSCE chairmanship was a state role, not a private award.
records.subject: Edi Rama

records.title: Albania–Israel: four numbers measuring different things
records.body: Albania’s embassy describes more than 45 Israeli companies in the market. RTSH reports about €19m of Israeli investment in the first nine months of 2025 and roughly €37m of bilateral trade during 2025 (€10.4m exports and €27m imports). The government reports 40 companies attending a May 2026 summit.
records.limit: Company counts, event attendance, investment flows and trade are different measures. These figures are attributed, not independently reconciled to QKB or Bank of Albania microdata. A press claim of 105 companies remains unverified; do not combine the counts.
records.subject: Albania–Israel trade

records.title: Timak Defence, Advanced Arms Technology and Ron Yeffet
records.body: Exit reports Ron Yeffet’s involvement in public/private defence ventures including Timak Defence and Advanced Arms Technology. Balkanweb reports SPAK registration of suspected procurement-related offences following searches involving Yeffet and Ardi Veliu.
records.limit: This is attributed reporting, not a conviction. Obtain each entity’s current cap table, tender ID, direct-award basis, invoice and response. A reported 20% state interest is not proof that every payment or company has the same ownership. The draft Euronews Albania link returned 404 in this check.
records.subject: Timak / AAT

records.title: Elbit/KAYO: the Vlorë aviation memorandum
records.body: Albania’s Defence Ministry announced an April 2025 memorandum involving Elbit Systems and KAYO to revive aviation training in Vlorë, with Rama, Balluku and Vengu at the ceremony.
records.limit: A memorandum and attendance do not establish a completed procurement, payment, airport-concession takeover or transfer of land. Those require separate signed records.
records.subject: Elbit / KAYO

records.title: JET Bank: parent-company shares need registry reconciliation
records.body: InfoNews reporting describes 71.52% of Dutch JET Holdings through Cyprus Constador Ltd, linked to Idan Avishai. A second report attributes parent holdings to Israel Albania Holdings (12.4%), Nathan Lawrence (4.9%), Yebogogo (4.9%), DON Albania Holdings (3.7%) and Ori Eyal (2.6%).
records.limit: These remain reported parent-company interests, not independently certified current direct bank shares. Rounded figures need reconciliation. Obtain Dutch, Cyprus and Israeli filings and Bank of Albania licensing disclosures before asserting ultimate control or source of capital.
records.subject: JET Bank

records.title: H.A.P.I, TEDA and the ADC data-centre proposal
records.body: RTSH reports a TEDA agreement with H.A.P.I Advanced Technologies. A separate Voxnews report describes a proposed €100m ADC data centre with Happy Technologies (80%) and DIT (20%), naming Roi Shaposhnik, Noam Frank, Shlomi Avni, Itai Melchior, Zvika Friedman, Nir Poltorak and Dan Carmi in corporate roles.
records.limit: The TEDA-wide €100m figure is not automatically H.A.P.I’s committed capital. ADC’s ownership, lease, permit and financing remain reporting-led until original records are obtained. A proposed investment is not money already spent.
records.subject: H.A.P.I / TEDA

records.title: Energy, agriculture and an investment-company lead
records.body: Albania’s embassy identifies Electrical Grid Monitoring and Powercom in electricity-sector cooperation and describes a historical €2m Yesh Albania agriculture investment. The research also identifies Albanian Israel Development & Investment Corporation (M12026018L) and reported historical shares of Damian Brikman (66%) and Riza Arshiaj (34%).
records.limit: Embassy statements are not the concession contracts or audited payments. The latter company’s certified extract was not obtained in this review; business objects do not establish executed developments or ownership of any parcel.
records.subject: Powercom / EGM

records.title: Vlorë’s Jewish Museum: cultural project and procurement
records.body: AADF lists a $6.5m committed budget for the Albanian Jewish Museum. The government names Tel Aviv’s Kimmel Eshkolot Architects as the winning design studio. AADF’s construction tender 00186 is publicly listed.
records.limit: The draft’s $3m excluding-VAT tender ceiling was not independently extracted from the tender attachments here. AADF is an Albanian-American foundation; a design commission or Jewish heritage project does not establish Israeli state ownership or territorial transfer.
records.subject: AADF / museum

records.title: Land, broadcasters and further company names
records.body: Media compilations name Roots, Farmalabacy, Taga Urbanic, Sonovia, Arrow Operations and Technologies, Top Green House, Isal Tech Black Powder, BPG Albania, Trilogic Financial Solutions, D&A Holdings, Homeport Albania, AMA Export AL, Reach and SeaSun Albania Capital. They are retained as an unverified research queue.
records.limit: Do not count them as verified Israeli-owned firms without entity IDs and dated ownership records. No specific major broadcaster was verified as Israeli-owned in this round. Use AMA/Media Ownership Monitor and QKB; landholding requires a parcel and title. Names, religion and editorial positions are not ownership evidence.
records.subject: Company research leads

records.title: Bilateral agreements: public diplomacy, not covert-control evidence
records.body: The Israeli embassy’s chronology lists investment protection (1996), trade/agriculture (2001), AIDA–Israel Export Institute cooperation (2015), airport/security arrangements (2018), cybersecurity (2023), tourism and Sheba oncology cooperation (2024), and health cooperation (2025).
records.limit: An official chronology confirms the embassy’s account of agreements; it does not identify every implementing contract, payment or company beneficiary. Israeli state bodies, citizens, incorporated firms and Jewish religious or heritage organisations are distinct categories.
records.subject: Bilateral agreements

records.title: Cross-border investigations: Europol and Eurojust
records.body: Europol describes ten arrests on 7–8 August 2025 in an investigation of cocaine routes from Latin America through Hamburg and Rotterdam, supported by Sky ECC evidence and asset seizures. Eurojust’s May 2026 release describes 12 arrests, three summonses and five Italy–Albania joint teams operating between 2018 and 2026, with more than 170 arrests and seven tonnes seized across those teams.
records.limit: These are separate investigations, not proof of a single hierarchy or the guilt of all suspects. Arrest, charge, seizure and conviction must remain distinct. Ethnic Albanians collectively are not implicated.
records.subject: Europol / Eurojust

records.title: Dritan Gjika: alleged trafficking and asset orders
records.body: OCCRP/Shteg’s 18 June 2026 report describes SPAK allegations against Dritan Gjika and others involving Latin American and European cocaine routes, with seizure action concerning approximately €150m in assets. It reports his May 2025 arrest in Abu Dhabi and Ecuadorian proceedings.
records.limit: The source describes allegations and proceedings, not a personal final conviction established here. OCCRP says his lawyers did not respond to its request. Later extradition, appeal and confiscation outcomes require a dated court update.
records.subject: Dritan Gjika

records.title: Tahiri: the offence and denial matter
records.body: OCCRP’s 15 February 2022 report describes an appeals-court sentence of three years and four months for former interior minister Saimir Tahiri for abuse of office involving the Habilaj network. It also reports his acquittal on drug-trafficking charges and his denial of wrongdoing.
records.limit: This card describes that historical reported judgment, not a verified October 2026 custody or final-appeal status. Ministerial service under Rama establishes political accountability questions, not Rama’s participation in a criminal organisation.
records.subject: Saimir Tahiri

records.title: Ahmetaj, Koka and Bllako: separate case histories
records.body: Transparency International describes the incinerator investigations and allegations of corruption, laundering and concealed assets against former deputy prime minister Arben Ahmetaj. Its account includes his denial and claim of political revenge, a reported conviction of former environment minister Lefter Koka, and proceedings involving Alqi Bllako.
records.limit: The database is a historical case account and cannot establish every defendant’s latest appeal outcome. Do not merge the Tirana, Fier and Elbasan cases or label Ahmetaj convicted on this evidence. No direct criminal-payment link to Rama is established by these records.
records.subject: Separate prosecution histories

records.title: Enforcement progress belongs in the investigation too
records.body: The European Commission’s 2025 Albania report assesses the country as moderately prepared against organised crime and records good progress in relevant recommendations, including SPAK’s financial-investigation capacity, money-laundering work and seizures. It reports 25 Eurojust-supported joint teams between March 2024 and July 2025, including 16 concerning narcotics.
records.limit: The report also identifies implementation and operational weaknesses. Successful enforcement and exposure of wrongdoing can coexist; neither a prosecution nor a country assessment alone settles individual guilt.
records.subject: Enforcement assessments

records.title: OSF/OSFA: what the foundation says it funded
records.body: Open Society’s Albania factsheet says work began in 1992, with over $57m for rebuilding 275 schools and kindergartens in the 1990s and $600,000 earmarked in 2015 for judicial-reform expertise and consultation. Alex Soros is listed as chair of the OSF board.
records.limit: These are the foundation’s own program figures. The $600,000 is an earmark, not a verified list of payments to individuals. Swiss-funded LëvizAlbania cooperation must remain separate from OSF’s own funding and worldwide expenditure.
records.subject: OSF / OSFA

records.title: 2024 grants: two paid entries checked against the filing
records.body: The Foundation to Promote Open Society’s 2024 Form 990-PF (EIN 26-3753801), Part XIV 3(a), PDF page 12, lists general-support payments to Open Society Foundation for Albania of $2,560,000 and $3,347,000. Together these entries total $5,907,000. They appear in the paid-during-the-year section.
records.limit: This is a sum of two entries from one grantmaker, not total philanthropic spending in Albania. It is not a personal payment to Rama or a link to a public tender. Do not add these entries to overlapping multiyear totals.
records.subject: Open Society grant filing

records.title: Grant-index totals located; annual reconciliation still open
records.body: The philanthropy.org index lists OSFA recipient aggregates of $4.7m across four grants in 2020–2021 and $15.7m across ten grants in 2022–2024. These index entries are now located, but not reconciled against the original annual schedules. The draft’s separate $26,535 individual 2023 grant remains uncorroborated.
records.limit: These are index-reported aggregates, not verified personal transfers or public tenders. Do not add the separately checked 2024 entries to the overlapping multi-year totals. Funding for other years remains unestablished; unknown does not mean zero.
records.subject: Unreconciled grant totals

records.title: Judicial Watch, USAID and OSF: identify the recipient first
records.body: Judicial Watch’s FOIA-based account alleges US government support for Soros-linked judicial-reform activity, including reported embassy survey cooperation and a $9m USAID/EWMI program. OSF’s February 2025 response denies receiving USAID funding or directing its budgets while acknowledging cooperation with donors.
records.limit: These accounts may concern different entities, years and funding flows. The $9m is not independently reconciled here and must not automatically be treated as an OSFA grant. Obtain award IDs, recipients, obligations and disbursements before describing a contradiction or adding amounts.
records.subject: USAID / EWMI

records.title: Treasury payments: useful totals, missing legal identifiers
records.body: Overit’s Ministry of Finance-derived snapshot covers 20 December 2024–5 December 2025. It lists Integrated Energy BV SPV at ALL 1,340m across 53 payments and six institutions, and TIMAK DEFENCE at ALL 1,048m across two payments and two institutions.
records.limit: Payee names lack NIPT identifiers in the source. These are name-labelled payment totals, not verified contract-by-contract matches or findings of illicit use. Open Spending supports further transaction research; the Open Contracting registry’s Albanian PPC dataset concerns complaints/decisions rather than all awards.
records.subject: Treasury payment records

records.title: 5D: contracts, profit and alleged ownership
records.body: Transparency International’s 5D account alleges indirect control by former municipal officials Redi Molla and Mariglen Qato through nominal owners. It reports ALL 2bn (about €20m) in contracts and ALL 200m (about €2m) net profit. Open Data Albania’s dossier identifies seizure-related interests including Restur and a 24% Mediterranean Investment Group stake held through Restur.
records.limit: The €20m measure is corrected from the draft’s inconsistent revenue label. Contract totals, profit and Treasury payments are different. Proceedings and seizures are not a final conviction established here. Neither this case nor incinerator cases establish an OSFA/Soros payment link.
records.subject: 5D contracts
connection: Alleged ownership; not a Soros link

records.title: Srebrenica: Albania voted yes
records.body: The UN recorded vote for resolution A/RES/78/282 on 23 May 2024 lists Albania as voting YES, Serbia NO and Israel as not voting. This contradicts the submitted claim that Albania did not vote.
records.limit: Rama–Vučić Open Balkan cooperation, Kosovo policy disagreements and sanctions alignment are separate questions. An ambiguous social-media statement cannot substitute for a dated official position.
records.subject: UN Srebrenica vote

records.title: Vlorë, emigration, housing and the unreviewed video
records.body: Community leads raise affordability, emigration, construction and laundering risks, Bektashi sovereignty and Vlorë projects. FES and GI-TOC research offer systemic context. The submitted TikTok link remains unreviewed: its speaker, context and specific claims have not been established.
records.limit: Population decline, first residence permits and diaspora ancestry are not interchangeable counts. Systemic laundering risks do not prove every development illicit. No evidence reviewed supports a coordinated territorial takeover by Jewish people or Israel, the claimed 90% historical Jewish population, or an intentional policy to force youth out.
records.subject: Community claims

records.title: Vlorë airport: reporting is not an award
records.body: The research points to airport-company records involving Mabco Constructions SA and 2A Group. A separate report about TIMAK AVIATION, Ron Yeffet and Arjeta Puca explicitly says it had not found an official takeover decision or contract.
records.limit: No airport-award or Israeli-state land-ownership edge is drawn. The registry links could not be fully retrieved in this check, and a report about a possible transaction does not establish a completed transfer.
records.subject: Vlorë airport

records.title: What is still needed to close the documentary gaps?
records.body: The research queue covers certified QKB/KvK ownership histories, Atlantic Incubation Partners disclosures, Sazan decision annexes and negotiation minutes, land valuations and demining payments, the Tirana concession and amendments, Llogara awards, Zvërnec permits and parcels, Durrës guarantees/accounts, and original grant schedules.
records.limit: No outreach or information request was sent during this review. Public comments and private submissions are leads, reviewed before publication. Private senders and screenshots are excluded from the public research. Join financial records using legal identifiers and dated documents, never names, photographs, religion or association alone.
records.subject: Document requests

records.title: OSFA’s legal registration and representative
records.body: OpenCorporates.al lists OSFA as an active nonprofit with identifier J62005011N, formation date 5 August 1996 and legal representative Andi Dobrushi. The listing records a last change on 21 February 2025.
records.limit: This is a registry-derived listing, not a newly certified QKB extract. The linked historical PDF could not be retrieved in this review. Legal formation in 1996 is distinct from the foundation’s account that its Albania work began in 1992.
records.subject: OSFA’s legal registration and representative

records.title: Who is listed on OSF Western Balkans leadership?
records.body: The organisation’s roster, checked on 24 October 2026, lists Andi Dobrushi as director, Miodrag Milosavljevic as deputy director and Dukagjin Hyseni as chief operating officer.
records.limit: This is the organisation’s own account. The review date is not an appointment date. A staff role does not establish political control, personal payments or responsibility for an unrelated project.
records.subject: Who is listed on OSF Western Balkans leadership?
connections: Listed deputy director; roster checked 24 October 2026
Listed chief operating officer; roster checked 24 October 2026

records.title: LëvizAlbania: historical consortium and a 2023 transition
records.body: LëvizAlbania describes a Swiss-funded project implemented by OSFA, Partners Albania for Change and Development, and Co-PLAN. Its site says that from 1 October 2023 the independent LëvizAlbania Center operates outside Swiss development-agency auspices.
records.limit: Swiss government material corroborates the historical consortium. Do not extend that arrangement into the present or infer that OSFA owns the other partners. This source does not establish a later funding contract.
records.subject: LëvizAlbania: historical consortium and a 2023 transition

records.title: Ahmetaj: the reported €491,000 allegation and denial
records.body: BIRN’s 15 July 2023 account of a prosecution file reports alleged benefits of at least €491,000 from businessmen Klodian Zoto and Mirel Mërtiri to Arben Ahmetaj. Transparency International summarises the allegation and records Ahmetaj’s denial and claim of political revenge.
records.limit: These are reported prosecutorial allegations, not proven payments or a final conviction. The amount describes a combined allegation, not a separate payment by each businessman. This historical reporting does not establish the current case outcome or a payment to Edi Rama.
records.subject: Ahmetaj: the reported €491,000 allegation and denial

records.title: A 2016 report on OSFA’s reform strategy
records.body: Exit’s 22 August 2016 article describes constitutional-reform advocacy in a document it identifies as OSFA’s 2014–2017 strategy. This establishes what Exit reported, rather than independent authentication of the underlying document.
records.limit: The linked document could not be independently accessed in this review. The article’s interpretation is attributed to the outlet; it does not prove ownership of the judiciary, bribery or control over individual judicial decisions.
records.subject: A 2016 report on OSFA’s reform strategy

records.title: The Ministry’s 2024 fiscal-risk statement
records.body: The Ministry of Finance’s Fiscal Risk Statement for 2024, published with a Tirana 2025 date, reports on public-private partnerships and concession exposure. Its table distinguishes actual expenditure, plans and forecasts, expressed in thousand ALL.
records.limit: Budget exposure is not proof of corruption or an individual payment. Keep actual and forecast figures separate; the report’s year and publication year are different. No project-specific total is inferred here.
records.subject: The Ministry’s 2024 fiscal-risk statement

records.title: Correspondence attributed to Rama and Veliaj
records.body: On 11 December 2023, CNA reported documents released by the Democratic Party: a 2016 bonus approval attributed to Edi Rama and 2017 letters attributed to Erion Veliaj concerning the Tirana concession procedure and fee.
records.limit: The letters and signatures were not independently authenticated in this review. The procurement register separately supports the bonus decision in R01; it does not authenticate these reproductions. Neither correspondence nor the outlet’s interpretation establishes criminal guilt.
records.subject: Correspondence attributed to Rama and Veliaj

events.title: Foundation’s historical funding account
events.body: Open Society’s Albania factsheet says work began in 1992, with over $57m for rebuilding 275 schools and kindergartens in the 1990s and $600,000 earmarked in 2015 for judicial-reform expertise and consultation. Alex Soros is listed as chair of the OSF board.
events.limit: These are the foundation’s own program figures. The $600,000 is an earmark, not a verified list of payments to individuals. Swiss-funded LëvizAlbania cooperation must remain separate from OSF’s own funding and worldwide expenditure.

events.title: OSFA’s legal registration and representative
events.body: OpenCorporates.al lists OSFA as an active nonprofit with identifier J62005011N, formation date 5 August 1996 and legal representative Andi Dobrushi. The listing records a last change on 21 February 2025.
events.limit: This is a registry-derived listing, not a newly certified QKB extract. The linked historical PDF could not be retrieved in this review. Legal formation in 1996 is distinct from the foundation’s account that its Albania work began in 1992.

events.title: Albania joins NATO
events.body: Albania joined NATO on 1 April 2009. Its collective-security commitments differ from Switzerland’s permanent neutrality. The research asks whether foreign-policy choices offer measurable humanitarian, diplomatic, economic and security benefits proportionate to their risks.
events.limit: Neutrality is not the absence of sanctions, diplomacy or refugee protection. The comparison is a political alternative to analyse, not evidence that Albania is legally required to follow Swiss policy.

events.title: MEK relocation announcement
events.body: The US State Department’s 18 March 2013 statement welcomed Prime Minister Sali Berisha’s offer to accept 210 former Camp Ashraf residents temporarily at Camp Hurriya, with UNAMI and UNHCR cooperation. The source link has been corrected. Later expansion under Rama and the Ashraf-3 context belong to the subsequent timeline.
events.limit: This establishes the initial offer and international support, not all later terms, expenditure or alleged MEK operations. It does not establish that Israel ordered the relocation.

events.title: Incinerator evaluation bonus
events.body: The Open Procurement register records an 8% evaluation bonus approved on 7 December 2016, one bidder, Integrated Energy B.V., and an offer of ALL 17,139,106,821 excluding VAT. The 30-year award is dated 24 August 2017; contract 6021 Rep., 2894 Kol. is dated 31 August 2017. The contracting authority was the Ministry of Environment.
events.limit: A bonus or a single bidder does not itself prove an offence. The offer is not the amount ultimately paid; performance, amendments and expenditure need separate records.

events.title: A meeting on the water
events.body: Kushner’s family trip brought him to Albania. In Rama’s later account, an invitation aboard a yacht in Durrës introduced the two men. Reporting dates the encounter to summer 2021.
events.limit: This is a retrospective account. The host’s identity is not consistently established; the meeting does not prove a financing arrangement.

events.title: The conversation turns to investment
events.body: According to the Financial Times account relayed by Politiko, a later conversation at Davos touched on Albania and investment opportunities.
events.limit: The exact date of this meeting is not established here. An expression of interest is not an agreement.

events.title: Reporting on Tahiri judgment
events.body: OCCRP’s 15 February 2022 report describes an appeals-court sentence of three years and four months for former interior minister Saimir Tahiri for abuse of office involving the Habilaj network. It also reports his acquittal on drug-trafficking charges and his denial of wrongdoing.
events.limit: This card describes that historical reported judgment, not a verified October 2026 custody or final-appeal status. Ministerial service under Rama establishes political accountability questions, not Rama’s participation in a criminal organisation.

events.title: Historical beneficial-owner extract
events.body: The registry-derived profile for Integrated Energy BV SPV (L72031013B) lists Dutch GeoGenix BV, formerly Integrated Energy B.V. (66671752), as its 100% parent. Its reproduced beneficial-owner extract effective 10 May 2022 identifies Alberto Presezzi at 40%, Max Abitbol at 20% and Dominique Marcelle Obadia Abitboll at 20%. Another 20% is not individually identified in that extract.
events.limit: These are historical indirect interests, not certified current ownership. Klodian Zoto’s former administrator role in 2016–2018 does not establish current ownership. Preventive seizure in 2023 and the January 2026 administrator listing for Indrit Karaj are separate legal facts.

events.title: Durrës Marina memorandum
events.body: The Port Authority records a 10 August 2022 memorandum between Eagle Hills, represented by Mohamed Alabbar, and Albanian Seaports Development Company, represented by Erlis Hereni. Research also identifies a reported 67%/33% project-vehicle split and a historical 40.18% indirect Alabbar interest in Eagle Hills.
events.limit: The latter percentages remain registry-verification leads in this release. The public return requires the signed agreement, land valuation, tax treatment, guarantees and accounts. No evidence reviewed establishes an award-for-contract exchange with the UAE presidency.

events.title: Cyberattack attribution
events.body: FBI/CISA’s AA22-264A advisory documents Iranian state-linked destructive cyber operations against Albanian government networks in 2022. AP separately reported Albanian authorities’ attribution of the February 2024 INSTAT attack to HomeLand Justice.
events.limit: Neither record proves that Iran organised October 2026 demonstrations. A new attribution needs identified accounts, operators, payments, communications and independent technical evidence. Online amplification, even if established, does not invalidate protesters’ grievances.

events.title: A return visit
events.body: Kushner returned with a larger group, including Richard Grenell. The same account describes a week of visits and explicit interest in investing.
events.limit: A visit establishes neither land ownership nor project approval.

events.title: Ahmetaj: the reported €491,000 allegation and denial
events.body: BIRN’s 15 July 2023 account of a prosecution file reports alleged benefits of at least €491,000 from businessmen Klodian Zoto and Mirel Mërtiri to Arben Ahmetaj. Transparency International summarises the allegation and records Ahmetaj’s denial and claim of political revenge.
events.limit: These are reported prosecutorial allegations, not proven payments or a final conviction. The amount describes a combined allegation, not a separate payment by each businessman. This historical reporting does not establish the current case outcome or a payment to Edi Rama.

events.title: LëvizAlbania: historical consortium and a 2023 transition
events.body: LëvizAlbania describes a Swiss-funded project implemented by OSFA, Partners Albania for Change and Development, and Co-PLAN. Its site says that from 1 October 2023 the independent LëvizAlbania Center operates outside Swiss development-agency auspices.
events.limit: Swiss government material corroborates the historical consortium. Do not extend that arrangement into the present or infer that OSFA owns the other partners. This source does not establish a later funding contract.

events.title: Two paid grant entries
events.body: The Foundation to Promote Open Society’s 2024 Form 990-PF (EIN 26-3753801), Part XIV 3(a), PDF page 12, lists general-support payments to Open Society Foundation for Albania of $2,560,000 and $3,347,000. Together these entries total $5,907,000. They appear in the paid-during-the-year section.
events.limit: This is a sum of two entries from one grantmaker, not total philanthropic spending in Albania. It is not a personal payment to Rama or a link to a public tender. Do not add these entries to overlapping multiyear totals.

events.title: UN General Assembly vote
events.body: The UN recorded vote for resolution A/RES/78/282 on 23 May 2024 lists Albania as voting YES, Serbia NO and Israel as not voting. This contradicts the submitted claim that Albania did not vote.
events.limit: Rama–Vučić Open Balkan cooperation, Kosovo policy disagreements and sanctions alignment are separate questions. An ambiguous social-media statement cannot substitute for a dated official position.

events.title: Sazan strategic-investor decision referenced
events.body: AIDA’s 2025 register of information requests and responses refers to Strategic Investment Committee Decision 23 of 30 December 2024 and Atlantic Incubation Partners LLC (EIN 92-3329707). It is an information-request register, not a complete strategic-investment or ownership register. Reuters reported strategic status for the proposed Kushner-linked resort.
events.limit: The signed decision, annexes and full ownership chain have not all been independently inspected. The registered agent Corporation Service Company is not thereby a beneficial owner. Strategic status is not proof of a completed land sale or construction.

events.title: Museum construction launch reported
events.body: AADF lists a $6.5m committed budget for the Albanian Jewish Museum. The government names Tel Aviv’s Kimmel Eshkolot Architects as the winning design studio. AADF’s construction tender 00186 is publicly listed.
events.limit: The draft’s $3m excluding-VAT tender ceiling was not independently extracted from the tender attachments here. AADF is an Albanian-American foundation; a design commission or Jewish heritage project does not establish Israeli state ownership or territorial transfer.

events.title: Elbit / KAYO memorandum
events.body: Albania’s Defence Ministry announced an April 2025 memorandum involving Elbit Systems and KAYO to revive aviation training in Vlorë, with Rama, Balluku and Vengu at the ceremony.
events.limit: A memorandum and attendance do not establish a completed procurement, payment, airport-concession takeover or transfer of land. Those require separate signed records.

events.title: Europol operation
events.body: Europol describes ten arrests on 7–8 August 2025 in an investigation of cocaine routes from Latin America through Hamburg and Rotterdam, supported by Sky ECC evidence and asset seizures. Eurojust’s May 2026 release describes 12 arrests, three summonses and five Italy–Albania joint teams operating between 2018 and 2026, with more than 170 arrests and seven tonnes seized across those teams.
events.limit: These are separate investigations, not proof of a single hierarchy or the guilt of all suspects. Arrest, charge, seizure and conviction must remain distinct. Ethnic Albanians collectively are not implicated.

events.title: SPAK statement on alleged tender interference
events.body: SPAK’s 20 November 2025 statement describes proceeding 136/2025 and alleged interference involving Belinda Balluku and five procurement-committee officials: Evis Berberi, Gentian Gjyli, Erald Elezi, Jetmira Dervishi and Mirzeta Kashnica. The construction tender ceiling was ALL 18,967,810,952 excluding VAT.
events.limit: A ceiling is not a payment and allegations are not convictions. Reuters reported further formal charges on 20 October 2026 and Balluku’s denial. The separate 2021 supervision tender and reported 2025 A-M/Gjoka maintenance award (about ALL 230m over four years) must not be attributed to the construction case without evidence.

events.title: Zvërnec development approval, government account
events.body: In its June 2026 explanation, the government said Sazan remained state property and no final agreement had then been signed. Its account of a 30 March development-permit approval and 15 May in-depth environmental assessment requirement concerns Zvërnec. Legal and technical conditions still governed issuance of the development permit.
events.limit: This is the government’s dated account, not an independent cadastral audit or a construction permit. Obtain each parcel, land title, environmental decision and final agreement separately. Citizens.al’s account of ten negotiation meetings led by Elira Kokona and reported state demining costs require minutes and expenditure records.

events.title: Sazan Operations incorporation reported
events.body: BIRN’s April 2026 reporting on QKB records describes Sazan Operations, founded 1 April 2026, as controlled through six companies by Ramez and Mohamad Al-Khayyat. It reports five unnamed Albanian investors holding 24% of Blue Industries Investment Holding BV, an entity in the related structure.
events.limit: That 24% must not be depicted as a direct stake in Sazan or Atlantic Incubation Partners. Kushner’s precise personal equity and the complete chain between project vehicles remain unverified. Citizenship and family connections do not establish state control or wrongdoing.

events.title: Bilateral business summit
events.body: Albania’s embassy describes more than 45 Israeli companies in the market. RTSH reports about €19m of Israeli investment in the first nine months of 2025 and roughly €37m of bilateral trade during 2025 (€10.4m exports and €27m imports). The government reports 40 companies attending a May 2026 summit.
events.limit: Company counts, event attendance, investment flows and trade are different measures. These figures are attributed, not independently reconciled to QKB or Bank of Albania microdata. A press claim of 105 companies remains unverified; do not combine the counts.

events.title: From the coast to the streets
events.body: OSW traces the environmental demonstrations to 30 May. By October, reporting describes broader student demands about education, living costs and accountability.
events.limit: Political support does not prove control of the movement. No reliable central financing account has been established here.

events.title: OCCRP reporting on Gjika allegations
events.body: OCCRP/Shteg’s 18 June 2026 report describes SPAK allegations against Dritan Gjika and others involving Latin American and European cocaine routes, with seizure action concerning approximately €150m in assets. It reports his May 2025 arrest in Abu Dhabi and Ecuadorian proceedings.
events.limit: The source describes allegations and proceedings, not a personal final conviction established here. OCCRP says his lawyers did not respond to its request. Later extradition, appeal and confiscation outcomes require a dated court update.

events.title: World Bank poverty brief: estimates and projection
events.body: The World Bank brief downloaded for this review is labelled October 2026. It estimates poverty at the $8.30/day line (2021 PPP) at 25.0% in 2024 and 23.1% in 2025, with a 21.6% projection for 2026. It says subsequent figures are model estimates because the latest household survey used for this measure is from 2018.
events.limit: This replaces the draft’s 23.8% for 2024 and October 2025 label. International poverty, national poverty and relative at-risk-of-poverty are different measures. The Macro Poverty Outlook provides wider economic context, not evidence of individual criminal responsibility.

events.title: Who is listed on OSF Western Balkans leadership?
events.body: The organisation’s roster, checked on 24 October 2026, lists Andi Dobrushi as director, Miodrag Milosavljevic as deputy director and Dukagjin Hyseni as chief operating officer.
events.limit: This is the organisation’s own account. The review date is not an appointment date. A staff role does not establish political control, personal payments or responsibility for an unrelated project.
